intro: Both, either and neither are for talking about two things or two people: “the two”, “one or the other”, “not one and not the other”. There are two big traps: we never say “the both”, and neither is already negative, so we do not use it with not.
objectifs: Use both, either and neither with a singular or plural noun, or with of + the/my/them.
Build both … and, either … or and neither … nor to join two things.
Put both in the right place in the sentence (We both like… / They are both…).
Avoid double negatives with neither, and choose “Neither of them…” instead of “Both of them don't…”.

texte: Both = the two (this one AND that one). Either = one or the other, it doesn't matter which. Neither = not this one and not that one.
These three words are only for TWO things or people. For three or more, use all, any and none (“none of my friends”).
Be careful with the noun: both takes a plural noun (both hands), but either and neither take a singular noun (either hand, neither hand).

lignes: Both hotels are near the beach.
You can sit at either table.
not one and not the other

exemples: Both my parents are teachers.
My father AND my mother.
You can pay by card or in cash. Either way is fine.
The two options are OK.
Neither bus goes to the airport.
Not one of the two buses; singular noun.

sections.titre: With of: both of, either of, neither of
texte: Before a determiner (the, my, these…) or a pronoun (us, you, them), use of: both of the films, either of my sisters, neither of them. The noun after of is always plural.
With both, of is optional before a noun: both my brothers = both of my brothers. But it is necessary before a pronoun: both of them (never “both them”).
After neither of / either of, the verb is singular in careful English (Neither of them is ready); the plural (Neither of them are ready) is very common in speech.
exemples: Both of us were tired after the trip.
of is necessary before us.
Do either of you speak Spanish?
One of you two, any one.
Neither of my brothers lives in Douala.
Singular verb (careful English).

texte: Both can also go after the subject, like an adverb: We both like jazz. It goes before the main verb, but after be and after an auxiliary: They are both students. We can both come.
At the end of a sentence, after an object pronoun: I love them both (= I love both of them).
We never say “the both”. Many languages use an article here, but English does not: both cities, not “the both cities”.
exemples: My sister and I both work in a bank.
Before the main verb.
The flats are both very expensive.
After be.
Here are two T-shirts. You can have them both.
After the object pronoun.

sections.titre: Both … and, either … or, neither … nor
texte: To join two things: both A and B (A and B together), either A or B (A or B, one of the two), neither A nor B (not A and not B).

Neither … nor is already negative, so the verb stays positive: Neither Paul nor Ana eats meat (not “doesn't eat”). With a negative verb, use either … or: He doesn't eat either meat or fish (= He eats neither meat nor fish).
The verb usually agrees with the nearest noun: Either my brother or my parents are coming.
exemples: She speaks both French and English.
The two languages.
We can meet either on Saturday or on Sunday.
One of the two days.
Neither Marc nor Sophie was at the meeting.
Not Marc and not Sophie; positive verb.

texte: To say “not one of the two”, use neither: Neither of them came. “Both of them didn't come” sounds strange and is not clear. In the same way, after not, use either: I don't like either of them (= I like neither of them).
In short answers, neither / either can stand alone: Tea or coffee? — Either, thanks. (any one) / Neither, thanks. (not one of them).
To agree with a negative sentence, say “Me neither” in informal speech. The full structure “Neither do I” comes in lesson 70.
exemples: Which one do you want, the red or the blue? — I don't mind. Either.
Any one of the two.
I don't like horror films. — Me neither.
I don't like them either.

formule: both + plural noun · either / neither + singular noun · both / either / neither of + the/my/them · both A and B · either A or B · neither A nor B (positive verb)
prononciation: both /bəʊθ/: the final “th” is voiceless /θ/, as in “think”. Don't say “bot”.
either: /ˈaɪðə/ (common in British English) or /ˈiːðə/ (common in American English). Both are correct.
neither: /ˈnaɪðə/ or /ˈniːðə/, with the voiced /ð/ of “the”.
nor /nɔː/ sounds like “more” with an n; no final r in British English.
In “neither … nor”, stress the two names: NEIther MARC nor soPHIE.
erreurs: Both hotels are full. / Both of the hotels are full.
Both of them are from Yaoundé. / They are both from Yaoundé.
Before a pronoun, of is necessary.
Neither is already negative: no double negative.
Neither Léa nor Tom don't drive.
With neither … nor, the verb stays positive.
Both of my brothers don't smoke.
For “not one of the two”, use neither.
Both goes before the main verb.
I don't like neither of them.
I don't like either of them. / I like neither of them.

dialogue.contexte: In a travel agency in Liège, Chloé and her husband cannot choose between two trips.
lignes: So, you can choose either Lisbon or Prague. Both trips are five days long.
We both love old cities. What's the difference?
Lisbon is by the sea, and Prague has beautiful bridges. Both of them are lovely in May.
Are the hotels in the centre?
Yes, both hotels are in the old town, and neither hotel is expensive.
I don't speak Portuguese or Czech.
Me neither! But neither language is a problem. People speak English in both cities.
That's right. Either city is a good choice.
either = any one of the two.
OK… Let's go to Lisbon this year and Prague next year!

mots: Both my sisters live in Montréal.
the two, this one and that one
not one and not the other
He drinks neither tea nor coffee.
the act of choosing; something you choose
We're planning a trip to Kribi.
a journey to a place and back
The twins both have curly hair.
two children born at the same time to the same mother
Tea or coffee? — I don't mind.
a road or route; a method

exercices.consigne: Complete with both, either or neither.
items: ___ my parents are from Bafoussam. (my father and my mother)
Both
You can come on Friday or Saturday. ___ day is OK for me.
Either
___ shop was open, so we went home. (not one of the two)
Neither
I have two brothers. ___ of them are doctors. (the two)
Both
The red bag or the black one? — ___. I don't like them. (not one of the two)
Neither
There are two buses to the station. You can take ___ of them.
either

exercices.consigne: Complete with of or Ø (nothing). Sometimes both are possible.
items: Both ___ them like football.
of
Neither ___ bike is new.
Ø
Either ___ my friends can help you.
of
Both ___ my cousins work in Lyon.
of or Ø (Both my cousins / Both of my cousins)

exercices.consigne: Rewrite with both … and, either … or or neither … nor.
items: Léa plays the guitar. Léa plays the piano.
Léa plays both the guitar and the piano.
Marc isn't at home. Sophie isn't at home.
Neither Marc nor Sophie is at home.
We can take the train, or we can take the car.
We can take either the train or the car.
The hotel is cheap. The hotel is comfortable.
The hotel is both cheap and comfortable.
He doesn't eat meat. He doesn't eat fish.
He eats neither meat nor fish.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Correct it.
items: The both girls are tall.
Both girls are tall. / Both of the girls are tall.
Neither of us didn't understand.
Neither of us understood.
They like both rice.
They both like rice.
Neither Paul nor Ana doesn't smoke.
Neither Paul nor Ana smokes.
Either answers is correct.
Either answer is correct.

exercices.consigne: Write one sentence for each situation.
items: You and your friend are tired. (both)
We are both tired. / Both of us are tired.
You have two brothers. Not one of them speaks German.
Neither of my brothers speaks German.
Someone asks: Tea or coffee? It's the same for you.
I don't mind. Either.
Your colleague speaks English and she speaks Spanish too.
She speaks both English and Spanish.

exercices.consigne: Think of two people in your family or two friends. Write four sentences: one with both, one with neither, one with either, and one with neither … nor.
items: Example answer
My two best friends are Awa and Kevin. They both live in Brussels. Neither of them has a car. I can call either of them when I need help. Neither Awa nor Kevin likes cold weather!

a_retenir: Both, either, neither: only for two things (otherwise all, any, none).
Both + plural noun; either / neither + singular noun; with of + the/my/them, plural noun.
Never “the both”; both of + pronoun (both of them); position: We both like… / They are both…
Neither is negative: no not with it. After not, use either.
Both A and B · either A or B · neither A nor B · Me neither = I don't either.
